uncited: Span space decomposition is a family of isosurface extraction methods that partition volume cells by mapping their extreme scalar values into a 2D coordinate system.
It differs from sibling methods by explicitly leveraging the geometric properties of min/max value pairs in a 2D plane rather than relying solely on hierarchical spatial subdivision of the domain.
The core mechanism of span space decomposition involves mapping each volume cell to a point in a 2D space based on its scalar field extrema.
where $f(v)$ is the scalar value at vertex $v$.
For a given isovalue $v$, a cell intersects the isosurface if and only if the isovalue lies strictly between the cell's minimum and maximum values.
The method relies on the observation that cells intersecting an isosurface can be identified by a 2D range query on their min/max values.
